source: Big Mike Danvers · Harbor City sports radio
passage: Folks, back in August I told you this would be a season of surprises, and look what happened. A rookie scored a hat trick in his first start, the coach got fired in October, and we beat the defending champs on the road. I called it, plain and simple. Next week I'll give you my playoff predictions, so stay tuned.
cue: I told you this would be a season of surprises, and look what happened
explanation: Mike's prediction was so vague that almost any season would fit it. He's choosing the surprising moments afterward and drawing his target around them.

whyNot.fal_cherry_picking: Mike isn't just hiding inconvenient games; his 'prediction' only becomes a hit because he defines it after seeing what happened.

passage: OK, look at the new album's tracklist. Take the first letter of tracks 2, 5, 7 and 11: T, O, U, R. TOUR! They hid the announcement right in front of us. I've been refreshing their site all morning. Fall tour dates incoming, calling it now.
cue: Take the first letter of tracks 2, 5, 7 and 11
explanation: The fan page chose which tracks to read only after hunting for a word. With a dozen titles to pick from, you can spell plenty of words by chance, so finding one proves nothing.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: No cause is being read into a correlation; the 'message' exists only because the tracks were chosen after the word was found.

passage:
Asha: I went through all six outages this year and tried every angle I could think of: weekday, time of day, deploys, weather, traffic, data center, vendor, who was on call.
Ryan: And?
Asha: Nothing lined up until on-call: four of the six were in Dmitri's weeks. That's our pattern. He's the common thread, and I'm flagging it to his manager.
cue: Nothing lined up until on-call: four of the six were in Dmitri's weeks. That's our pattern.
explanation: Asha sliced the outages eight different ways and kept the one slice that happened to fit. Check enough factors and one will line up by chance, so her 'pattern' is a target drawn around the hits.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: The deeper flaw isn't reading cause into a correlation; Asha found the 'link' only by testing factor after factor until one fit.

passage: We mapped all 40 dead songbirds reported in Fenwick County this spring, then circled the tightest bunch on the map: twelve birds in the northeast corner, around Millpond Road. Twelve in one small patch is way too many to be chance. Something there is harming birds, and we've asked the county to test the soil. Volunteers welcome for weekend counts!
cue: then circled the tightest bunch on the map: twelve birds in the northeast corner
explanation: The birders found the densest patch first and then drew their boundary around it. Scattered points always bunch up somewhere, so a circle drawn to fit the dots can't show that anything unusual is going on.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: No suspect is being blamed from a correlation; the 'hot spot' exists only because the circle was drawn around the dots after the fact.

title: Born in March? You may be destined for accounting
passage: Analyzing records of 50,000 workers in 60 professions, a team at the Halvorsen Institute compared every birth month against every job and found that people born in March were 18% more likely to become accountants. The researchers say early-spring births may shape a detail-oriented temperament.
cue: compared every birth month against every job
explanation: Comparing 12 months against 60 jobs makes 720 comparisons, and some are bound to stand out by chance. The team found its 'pattern' by searching, then told a story about why it fits.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: The causal story is a problem, but the deeper one is that the March link was picked out of hundreds of comparisons after the fact.

title: New sales forecast model
passage: Hi Tom, good news on the forecasting front. I tuned the new model on our last ten years of sales, adjusting the weights until it fit, and it now matches nine of those ten years almost exactly. That track record gives me a lot of confidence in its forecast of 14% growth next year. Happy to walk the team through it Thursday.
cue: adjusting the weights until it fit, and it now matches nine of those ten years
explanation: Priyanka shaped the model to fit the same ten years it now 'predicts', so matching them was guaranteed. That's drawing the target around past data, not a test of how well it forecasts.

whyNot.fal_cherry_picking: No unfavorable years are hidden; the model was simply fitted to the very data it's being credited with predicting.

title: Bus lanes cut Route 4 commute times, as planners predicted
passage: Before the bus lanes opened, city planners published their prediction: average Route 4 trips would fall by at least five minutes. Six months on, trips are 6.5 minutes faster, while Route 7, which got no lanes, is unchanged. The transport office says the results support keeping the lanes and adding them to Route 7.
cue: Before the bus lanes opened, city planners published their prediction
explanation: The target was drawn first: planners stated a specific prediction in advance, then checked it against a route without lanes. A hit on a target set beforehand is real evidence.

whyNot.fal_texas_sharpshooter: The prediction was published before the results came in, so the target wasn't painted around the outcome afterward.

source: Dr. Imogen Clarke, Westvale Health Department
title: Update: stomach illness cluster
passage: Last week we flagged a cluster of 12 stomach illness cases. Rather than assume a source, we interviewed every case and a matched group of healthy residents: 11 of the 12 sick people had eaten at the Ferry Street food stall, versus 2 of 40 healthy people. The lab then matched patients' bacteria to samples from the stall, so we're confident it's the source.
cue: we interviewed every case and a matched group of healthy residents
explanation: Dr. Clarke treats the cluster as a lead, then tests it by comparing sick and healthy residents and confirming with lab results. That turns a noticed pattern into solid evidence.

whyNot.fal_texas_sharpshooter: The cluster wasn't taken as proof; it was tested with a comparison group and lab matching before any conclusion.
